title: Remove From the End
statement: You are given `head`, the first node of a singly linked list, and a number `n`. **Remove the `n`-th node counting from the end** of the list (the last node is the 1st from the end) and return the head of the resulting list. `n` is never larger than the length of the list. (In the examples the list is shown as the list of its values.)

examples.explanation: The 2nd node from the end is 4, so it is removed.
Removing the only node leaves an empty list.

hints.nudge: If you knew the length, you would know which node to remove. Can you find the right spot in a single pass?
hints.pattern: Two pointers with a gap of n nodes between them.
hints.pseudocode:
dummy = node before head; fast = dummy; slow = dummy
move fast n steps forward
while fast.next: fast = fast.next; slow = slow.next
slow.next = slow.next.next
return dummy.next
hints.walkthrough: Counting the length first and then walking works in two passes. For one pass, start two pointers at a dummy node placed before the head. Move the fast pointer n steps ahead. Now move both pointers together until fast is at the last node: slow then stands right before the node to remove (the gap of n keeps it n nodes behind). Link slow past the removed node. The dummy node makes removing the head work without a special case.
